description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish staple, a comforting red lentil soup known for its rich flavor and velvety texture. This traditional recipe combines simple ingredients to create a nourishing and incredibly satisfying dish, often served with a vibrant chili-mint butter topping. It is a staple in every Turkish household, perfect for any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and carrot, and saute until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Do not let them brown too much.

instructions.title: Add Lentils and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Stir in the rinsed red lentils and tomato paste. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly to lightly toast the lentils and activate the tomato paste's flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Add salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pot from heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender.

instructions.title: Adjust Consistency and Seasoning
instructions.text: Return the soup to low heat. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint-Chili Butter
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (Pul Biber). Cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the prepared mint-chili butter. Serve immediately with a wedge of fresh lemon and crusty bread if desired.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, you can add a pinch of cumin or a bay leaf while the soup simmers, removing the bay leaf before blending.
Always rinse your red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear to remove any impurities and aid in digestion.
The mint-chili butter (tereyağlı nane ve pul biber) is crucial for an authentic Mercimek Corbasi experience; do not skip this flavorful topping.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi, a beloved staple of Turkish cuisine, is far more than just a simple soup. It's a hug in a bowl, a comforting embrace that nourishes the body and soul. This vibrant, creamy red lentil soup holds a special place in the hearts and on the tables of Turkish families, served from bustling street-side eateries to elegant dinner parties. Its humble ingredients belie a depth of flavor that is both satisfying and incredibly delicious. If you're looking to explore the rich tapestry of Turkish soups and stews, starting with Mercimek Corbasi is an absolute must.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi?

At its core, Mercimek Corbasi is a smooth, creamy soup made primarily from red lentils. Its distinctive reddish-orange hue comes from the lentils themselves, often enhanced by a touch of tomato paste. What truly sets this soup apart, however, is the delicate balance of earthy flavors from the lentils and vegetables, brightened by a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and a fragrant drizzle of mint-infused butter (or olive oil). It’s a versatile dish, equally at home as a hearty breakfast, a light lunch, or a comforting starter to a larger meal.

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its simplicity and accessibility. It requires basic pantry ingredients, is incredibly quick to prepare, and offers a powerhouse of nutrition. Rich in protein and fiber from the lentils, it’s naturally gluten-free and can easily be made vegan. Its comforting warmth makes it a popular choice year-round, but especially during colder months or as a soothing remedy when feeling under the weather. This Turkish Red Lentil Soup isn't just food; it's an experience, a taste of Turkish hospitality and tradition.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Creating an authentic Mercimek Corbasi requires a few key components, each playing a crucial role in building its signature flavor profile. The magic happens when these simple ingredients come together in harmony.

Here’s what you’ll typically need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Make sure to rinse them thoroughly before cooking.
*   **Olive Oil:** For sautéing vegetables and adding a rich base.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation, providing depth and savory notes.
*   **Carrot:** Adds a touch of sweetness and body to the soup. Some recipes also include potato for extra creaminess and starch.
*   **Tomato Paste:** Contributes umami, a subtle tang, and helps with the soup's beautiful color.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base. Broth will add more depth of flavor.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** Essential seasonings.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** A non-negotiable ingredient, providing a unique freshness and aroma.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Pepper):** Adds a mild warmth and vibrant color, especially in the final drizzle. Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Butter (or more Olive Oil):** For the final, crucial mint and pepper drizzle.
*   **Fresh Lemon:** Served alongside, a squeeze of lemon juice at the end brightens all the flavors.

These ingredients, when combined with care, transform into the irresistible Turkish Red Lentil Soup that has captivated palates worldwide.

## Step-by-Step Mercimek Corbasi Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is straightforward, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps to create your own delicious bowl of Turkish comfort.

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing your red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, preventing the soup from becoming overly cloudy or gummy. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and chopped carrot (and potato, if using) and cook for another 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step, known as "cooking out" the tomato paste, deepens its flavor and removes any raw taste.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot. Pour in the water or vegetable broth, then season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend to Perfection:** Once the lentils and vegetables are cooked through, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a standard blender (be cautious when blending hot liquids) and then return it to the pot. If the soup is too thick, you can add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency.
6.  **Prepare the Drizzle:** In a small pan, melt the butter (or heat olive oil) over low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes. Sizzle for about 30 seconds to a minute, being careful not to burn the spices. This fragrant oil is the signature finish.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the spiced mint butter over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

## Pro Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that perfect, authentic taste of Mercimek Corbasi is easy with a few insider tips:

*   **Rinse Those Lentils!** Don't skip this step. Rinsing removes starch and ensures a clearer, better-tasting soup.
*   **Sautéing is Key:** Take your time sautéing the onions, garlic, and carrots. Building a good flavor base here makes a huge difference.
*   **Don't Skimp on Tomato Paste:** Use good quality tomato paste and cook it for a minute or two to deepen its flavor.
*   **Blend It Smooth:** An immersion blender is a game-changer for achieving that silky-smooth texture without extra dishes. If you prefer a slightly chunkier soup, blend less.
*   **The Mint Drizzle is Essential:** The *nane yağı* (mint oil) is not just a garnish; it's a critical flavor component. The heat releases the aroma of the dried mint and the subtle warmth of the red pepper flakes, transforming the soup.
*   **Fresh Lemon is a Must:** Always serve with lemon wedges. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end brightens all the flavors and adds a crucial tangy counterpoint.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, or even add a pinch more dried mint if needed.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and pairs well with a variety of accompaniments. While delicious on its own, these additions elevate the dining experience:

*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** This is non-negotiable. A generous squeeze of lemon juice truly awakens the flavors of the Turkish Red Lentil Soup.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A warm, crusty loaf of bread, such as Turkish pide, simit, or even a good baguette, is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop.
*   **Turkish Pickles (Turşu):** The tangy crunch of mixed pickles provides a wonderful contrast to the creamy soup.
*   **Simple Salad:** A fresh shepherd's salad (çoban salatası) with tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and a lemon-olive oil dressing makes a light and refreshing side.
*   **Yogurt:** Some people enjoy a dollop of plain yogurt swirled into their soup, adding a cooling creaminess.
*   **As a Starter:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent first course for any Turkish meal, preparing the palate for richer dishes to come.

## Variations and Substitutions for Mercimek Corbasi

While the classic recipe is perfect, Mercimek Corbasi can be adapted to suit different tastes and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetable Additions:** Feel free to add other finely diced vegetables like celery, bell peppers, or even a small zucchini for extra nutrition and flavor.
*   **Spice It Up:** For a spicier kick, increase the amount of red pepper flakes in the drizzle, or add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the soup itself. A hint of cumin can also be added for an earthier flavor profile, though it's not traditional.
*   **Broth vs. Water:** While water is commonly used, vegetable broth will undoubtedly add more depth and richness to the soup.
*   **Vegan Option:** The soup is naturally vegetarian. To make it strictly vegan, simply substitute the butter in the final drizzle with extra olive oil or a plant-based butter alternative.
*   **Herb Variations:** While dried mint is paramount, a sprinkle of fresh parsley or dill as a garnish can add another layer of freshness.
*   **Consistency Control:** If you prefer a thicker soup, reduce the amount of liquid or simmer it for a longer period after blending. For a thinner consistency, simply add more hot water or broth.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's a culinary journey to the heart of Turkey. Its comforting warmth, vibrant flavors, and simple preparation make it an ideal dish for any occasion. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a soothing remedy, or simply a taste of authentic Turkish cuisine, this Turkish Red Lentil Soup is sure to become a cherished favorite in your kitchen. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the magic of Mercimek Corbasi.
